groups.title: Federal revenues, FY2024-25 – Public Accounts of Canada 2025, Vol. II, Section 1 (amounts published in $ thousands; shown here in $ millions)

defaults.basis: Full accrual basis, consolidated financial statements of the Government of Canada

observations.locator: Tax revenues – Income tax: Personal (also Vol. I Table 3.2: 234,319)
Tax revenues – Income tax: Corporate (also Vol. I Table 3.2: 96,954)
Tax revenues – Income tax: Non-resident (also Vol. I Table 3.2: 13,528)
Tax revenues – Other taxes and duties: Goods and services tax (also Vol. I Table 3.2: 52,503)
observations.caveat: Federal share only. In HST provinces the provincial part is collected for the province and is not federal revenue. Reported net of GST/HST rebates and credits.

observations.locator: Tax revenues – Excise tax: Gasoline 4,360.7 + Aviation gasoline and diesel fuel 1,289.4 (Vol. I Table 3.2 'Energy taxes': 5,650)
observations.caveat: FY2024-25 is before the April 2026 suspension of this tax; current-year revenue will be far lower.

observations.locator: Tax revenues – Other taxes and duties: Excise duties
observations.coverageNote: Public Accounts do not itemise alcohol, tobacco and cannabis separately in this line.

observations.locator: Tax revenues – Other taxes and duties: Air travellers security charge
Tax revenues – Other taxes and duties: Customs import duties (Vol. I Table 3.2: 6,264)
observations.caveat: Counter-tariff surtaxes began 4 March 2025, so only the final month of FY2024-25 reflects them.

observations.locator: Employment insurance premiums
Pollution pricing proceeds
observations.coverageNote: Pollution pricing proceeds include the fuel charge ($13.5 billion per the Annual Financial Report) plus small industrial pricing proceeds.
observations.caveat: The charge was set to zero from 1 April 2025, so this is historical revenue. Most proceeds were returned to households through rebates that are recorded as expenses.

groups.title: Canada Pension Plan – outside federal budgetary revenues

observations.basis: CPP Account financial statements, total contributions (base and additional CPP)
observations.locator: Annual report highlights: 'CPP contributions totalled $81.6 billion'
observations.caveat: One fiscal year earlier than the Public Accounts figures because the FY2024-25 CPP annual report was not yet available. Excludes the Québec Pension Plan.

Taxes on income, profits and capital gains payable by corporations and other enterprises [1112], sum of 13 jurisdictions

groups.title: Municipal and local government revenue, 2024 reference year – Statistics Canada Table 10-10-0020-01

defaults.basis: Statistics Canada government finance statistics (accrual, local governments)

observations.locator: Recurrent taxes on immovable property [1131], sum of 13 jurisdictions (includes real property taxes 61,018, business property taxes 313 and payments in lieu 2,796)
Other taxes on property [1133, 1134, 1136], sum of 13 jurisdictions
observations.coverageNote: The published category groups land transfer taxes with other minor property taxes; land transfer taxes alone are not separated.

observations.locator: Taxes on use of goods and on permission to use goods or perform activities [11451, 11452], sum of 13 jurisdictions
Taxes on specific services [1144], sum of 13 jurisdictions
observations.coverageNote: Taxes on specific services include accommodation taxes and any other service-specific municipal taxes.

groups.title: Provincial resource royalties – not part of the tax total

defaults.basis: Statistics Canada government finance statistics (accrual, general government sector)

observations.locator: Oil and gas royalties 24,507 + Forestry 877 + Mineral 687 + Water power 1,773 [1415], sum of 13 jurisdictions
observations.caveat: Resource royalties are property income in Statistics Canada’s classification, not taxes, so they lie outside the national total and keep the neutral size.

groups.title: Municipal user fees – not part of the tax total

defaults.basis: Statistics Canada government finance statistics (accrual, local governments)

observations.locator: Sales of goods and services [142], sum of 13 jurisdictions
observations.coverageNote: Includes all municipal sales of goods and services (utilities, transit fares, recreation, rentals), not only fees set by by-law.
observations.caveat: User fees and utility charges are sales of goods and services, not taxes, so they lie outside the national total and keep the neutral size.

unavailable.reason: Statistics Canada does not identify development charges as a separate line in its local-government revenue table; they are reported within other revenue categories.
